admission.authority: direct user continuation of the main-backed BRC multiplier transport and state-dependent scan-reduction program
admission.reason: Generalize the exact p=2 dynamic multiplier reduction to every square divisor visible simultaneously in the retained BRC ceiling root, while reusing canonical multiplier squarefree decomposition and odd-N scan typing.

methods.name: BRC multiplier square-content scan reduction
capabilities: exact one-shot stripping of every multiplier square factor whose root divides the known BRC ceiling root
exact immediate-ceiling witness preservation under m->m/g^2 and x->x/g
same gcd-factor preservation under declared gcd(n,m)=1
canonical reuse of m=a^2 d squarefree decomposition
composition with the existing exact odd-N 2-adic state representative
state-level IRREDUNDANT/REDUCED/IMPOSSIBLE classification before gap squarehood testing
methods.core_law: Write m=a^2 d with d squarefree and x=ceil(sqrt(mn)). Under gcd(n,m)=1, g=gcd(a,x) divides the square root y of every successful completion gap y^2=x^2-mn. Dividing m,x,y by g^2,g,g yields the exact immediate ceiling witness at m/g^2, and gcd(x-y,n)=gcd(x/g-y/g,n). After this one-shot normalization gcd(a/g,x/g)=1, so all square content visible in the current ceiling root has been removed.
methods.hard_boundary: Requires an already-known exact ceiling root and declared gcd(n,m)=1; a nontrivial multiplier gcd should be handled as a factor witness before this reduction. Squareful multipliers are not statically discardable: states with gcd(square-content-root,ceiling-root)=1 can be genuine first hits. Common-factor scaling is elementary prior art; no novelty priority, asymptotic factorization speedup, or Foundation promotion is claimed.
